cohort: A total of 293 mother-newborn dyads who experienced childbirth between 2015 and 2018 were included.
finding: The use of obstetric forceps (OF) is presented as an effective and safe method of vaginal operative delivery, resulting in a significantly lower frequency of newborn cephalohematoma compared to vacuum extraction (VE), despite a higher rate of maternal vaginal lacerations with OF.
mod_finding: Obstetric forceps is an effective and safe method of vaginal operative delivery, associated with 3.5 times fewer newborn cephalohematomas than vacuum extraction, though it leads to more maternal vaginal lacerations.
